title: On the mountain (Matthew 17:1–8)
hook: Peter, James and John see him shining and want to stay up there
carry: you can't stay on the mountain

segments.voice: Yesterday, walking on the water: egō eimi, it is I, and Peter sank, and was caught. Your line was the hand is already there. Today Peter is on a mountain, and he never wants to come down.

Think of a moment when everything was clear: a night under the stars, a wedding, the hour after a baby was born, a retreat where, for once, God felt close. You didn't want it to end; you wanted to build a little house right there and live in it. Jesus takes three friends, Peter, James and John, up a high mountain. And there, in front of them, something happens that they'll spend the rest of their lives trying to describe.
screen: `A MOMENT WHEN EVERYTHING WAS CLEAR.` → `THREE FRIENDS, A HIGH MOUNTAIN.` → `SOMETHING HAPPENS.`

segments.voice: In the Douay-Rheims: "And he was transfigured before them. And his face did shine as the sun: and his garments became white as snow." The Greek word is metamorphōthē, the root of our word metamorphosis. His form changed. For a moment, the three see him as he is. And he's not alone. Moses and Elijah appear, talking with him: Moses, who gave the Law, and Elijah, the great prophet. The whole story of Israel, standing beside him. Peter, overwhelmed, says the most human thing in the chapter: "Lord, it is good for us to be here." If you want, he says, I'll make three tents: one for you, one for Moses, one for Elijah. Let's stay. Mark adds, kindly, that Peter didn't know what to say, because they were terrified. While he's still talking, a bright cloud covers them, and a voice says what it said at the river on the day of the baptism, with three words more: "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased: hear ye him." Listen to him. The three fall on their faces in fear. Then Jesus comes, touches them, and says: arise, and fear not. They look up, and they see no one but Jesus alone. And they go back down the mountain, because down there is where the work is. The Church keeps the Transfiguration as a feast on August sixth, and reads this Gospel on the Second Sunday of Lent, a glimpse of the glory before the road to the cross. It's the fourth Luminous Mystery of the rosary. Tradition places it on Mount Tabor in Galilee; Matthew doesn't name the mountain.
screen: `HIS FACE SHONE AS THE SUN.` · `MOSES AND ELIJAH BESIDE HIM.` · `LET'S BUILD THREE TENTS.` · `HEAR YE HIM. THEN, DOWN THE HILL.` · then, large: `LORD, IT IS GOOD FOR US TO BE HERE.`

segments.voice: Let one bright memory come back, a moment when things felt whole, or holy, or simply good, and without analyzing it, stand in it again and notice what it felt like in your body. Then notice that you came down from it, and you're still carrying something from it. If you pray, you can thank God for that moment.
Transfiguration. From the Latin for a change of form: Jesus shining on the mountain before three friends. Today's word.
Your line: you can't stay on the mountain. But something comes down with you. Day fifty-two, in the books.
